candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes an enforceable numeric percent-solids limit; different readings of 'percent solids,' 'prior to mixing with other materials,' or whether sludge qualifies as containing unstabilized primary solids could change which limit applies or whether a reported measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether Alternative 8 applies at all; a different interpretation of 'treated' or what counts as unstabilized organic material could change whether the 90% limit is in force, whether related monitoring obligations attach, and how missing or conditional evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be injected below the surface of the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a conditional operational requirement tied to the injection pathway; whether this alternative governs a facility or event affects which permit obligations are applicable and how no-result or no-discharge evidence should be read.

candidates.exact_span: No significant amount of the sewage sludge shall be present on the land surface within one hour after the sewage sludge is injected.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a one-hour surface-presence standard whose operative meaning of 'significant amount' is interpretive; different readings could change compliance comparisons, whether monitoring or inspection evidence was required, and whether absent data reflects a documented no-violation state or unresolved obligation.

candidates.exact_span: When sewage sludge that is injected below the surface of the land is Class A with respect to pathogens, the sewage sludge shall be injected below the land surface within eight hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes an eight-hour timing limit conditioned on Class A pathogen status; interpretation of Class A classification, 'discharged from the pathogen treatment process,' and elapsed time could change limit applicability, monitoring expectations, and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge applied to the land surface or placed on a surface disposal site shall be incorporated into the soil within six hours after application to or placement on the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a six-hour incorporation requirement for surface application or surface disposal; different readings of application method, incorporation timing, or whether the site is a surface disposal site could change applicable limits, monitoring duties, and how absent timing evidence is treated.

candidates.exact_span: When sewage sludge that is incorporated into the soil is Class A with respect to pathogens, the sewage sludge shall be applied to or placed on the land within eight hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes an eight-hour post-treatment application limit for Class A sludge under the incorporation pathway; interpretation of Class A status and process discharge timing could change numeric compliance evaluation, monitoring applicability, and missing-data semantics.

candidates.exact_span: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Test - Once/Permit Life, performed within one year from the effective date of the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Declares a permit-life TCLP monitoring obligation with a one-year startup deadline; different readings of permit effective date, whether the test was ever required, or whether evidence satisfies the deadline could change required-monitoring determinations and missing-evidence classification.

Establishes an annual PCB monitoring frequency; interpretation of whether this requirement was in force for a given FY2025 period or whether reported or missing PCB results satisfy the obligation could change monitoring-applicability and no-result analyses.

candidates.exact_span: All other pollutants shall be monitored at the frequency shown below:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the scope of pollutants subject to tiered frequency requirements; what counts as an 'other pollutant' versus those with separate stated requirements could change which monitoring obligations are evaluated and how missing results are categorized.

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, monitoring frequency table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets annual monitoring for the lowest sludge-volume tier; boundary interpretation of the 0–290 metric-ton range could change the required frequency assigned to a facility or period.

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, monitoring frequency table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets quarterly monitoring for the middle sludge-volume tier; whether sludge quantity falls inside or outside the 290 and 1,500 metric-ton bounds could change required monitoring frequency.

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, monitoring frequency table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets bi-monthly monitoring for a higher sludge-volume tier; tier-boundary interpretation could change how many monitoring events were required in FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, monitoring frequency table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets monthly monitoring for the highest sludge-volume tier; whether quantity meets the 15,000 metric-ton threshold could materially change monitoring obligations and missing-evidence expectations.

candidates.exact_span: *Either the amount of bulk sewage sludge applied to the land or the amount of sewage sludge received by a person who prepares sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which sludge quantity metric controls tier selection and requires dry-weight basis; choosing applied bulk amount versus received prepared-sludge amount, or how dry weight is calculated, could change the applicable monitoring frequency and whether absent results indicate unmet obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Representative samples of sewage sludge shall be collected and analyzed in accordance with the methods referenced in 40 CFR 503.8(b).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prescribes sampling representativeness and analytical methods; interpretation of whether reported measurements were collected and analyzed under these methods could affect limit-comparison validity, monitoring-compliance findings, and whether missing or nonconforming data leave cases unresolved.

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, Section II introductory paragraph
candidates.exact_span: For those permittees meeting Class A or B pathogen reduction requirements and that meet the cumulative loading rates in Table 2 below, or the Class B pathogen reduction requirements and contain
candidates.computation_change_reason: States an applicability gate for Section II requirements tied to pathogen class and Table 2 or Table 3 conditions; different readings of whether a permittee satisfies Class A/B status, cumulative loading limits, or pollutant-concentration thresholds could change which limits, monitoring duties, and missing-evidence rules are in scope.
